description: POST /pss/send answers recorded from the Ant release the browser pins (scripts/fetch-ant.js), for #1062.
antd ran on loopback with no peers, chain or caches (--no-peerstore --no-disk-cache --gnosis-logs-rpc-url "" and an unreachable bootnode), so it holds no postage batch.
Ant checks the recipient before the batch: a recipient it can parse gets the batch error, one it cannot gets "invalid recipient public key".
The key is the public key of private key 0x1111...11 (32 bytes of 0x11).

exchanges.name: compressed66
exchanges.recipientForm: the compressed SEC1 key (33 bytes), what Freedom sends now

exchanges.name: compressed66Upper
exchanges.recipientForm: the same key in upper case

exchanges.name: uncompressed130
exchanges.recipientForm: the uncompressed SEC1 key (65 bytes, 04 prefix)

exchanges.name: xy128
exchanges.recipientForm: the 64-byte x || y that a bee-js PublicKey holds, with no SEC1 prefix

exchanges.name: objectObject
exchanges.recipientForm: what bee-js 13.2.0 pssSend actually puts in the query: its request options are deep-merged into plain objects, so the PublicKey prints as [object Object]
